factual_claims.claim: Colorado passed the first comprehensive U.S. state AI law, SB 24-205, in May 2024.
Colorado's SB 24-205 effective date was delayed from February 1 to June 30, 2026.
In March 2026, a Colorado working group released a draft 'repeal-and-replace' framework for SB 24-205.
The Trump administration's December 2025 executive order cited Colorado's SB 24-205 by name.
factual_claims.claim_label: Trump EO Cites Colorado AI Law

factual_claims.claim: The European Commission proposed the Digital Omnibus on AI in November 2025.
The EU Council agreed its negotiating position on the Digital Omnibus in March 2026.
factual_claims.claim_label: EU Council Agrees Digital Omnibus Position

factual_claims.claim: High-risk AI system requirements of the EU AI Act were originally set to apply beginning August 2, 2026.
factual_claims.claim_label: EU AI Act High-Risk Requirements Original Date

factual_claims.claim: The Digital Omnibus proposes backstop deadlines of December 2, 2027, for standalone high-risk systems and August 2, 2028, for AI embedded in regulated products.
factual_claims.claim_label: EU AI Act High-Risk Requirements New Deadlines

factual_claims.claim: Canada's Bill C-27, containing the Artificial Intelligence and Data Act, died on the order paper in January 2025.
In March 2026, UK Science Minister Patrick Vallance confirmed to parliament that there is no bill at the moment on AI regulation.
The EU withdrew the AI Liability Directive in February 2025.
The Biden administration's Executive Order 14110 on AI safety was revoked on President Trump's first day in office (assumed January 20, 2025).

A subsequent executive order, issued three days after Trump's inauguration, prompted the Office of Management and Budget to reissue federal guidance on the use (OMB Memorandum M-25-21) and acquisition (M-25-22) of AI in government.
factual_claims.claim_label: Trump EO on Federal AI Guidance

factual_claims.claim: Another executive order, issued December 2025, deploys the DOJ AI Litigation Task Force, conditions federal broadband funding on state AI policy alignment, and directs the FTC to issue guidance framing state bias mitigation requirements as potentially deceptive under federal law.
factual_claims.claim_label: Trump EO on State AI Laws and FTC Guidance

factual_claims.claim: The Senate voted 99-1 in July 2025 to strip a proposed 10-year moratorium on new state AI laws from federal reconciliation legislation.
factual_claims.claim_label: Senate Vote on State AI Law Moratorium

factual_claims.claim: The NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) was released in January 2023.
Within 18 months of its release, the NIST AI RMF appeared in executive orders, state AI legislation, and federal contractor requirements.
